title: Architecture overview
summary: Five harmonic-shaping families with eight variants, plus a separate Class-B comparison baseline. Auxiliary controls exist only in families with an independent physical tuning network.
actions: Inspect the family graph. Characterize the target binding and calibrate all adopted controls before comparison.

title: Hegazi tail/top/voltage: tail harmonic filter, aux = 2f tail tuning
summary: Explicit source or bias return filtering can change tail-noise transfer and the harmonic return. Calibrate the auxiliary network over the adopted main controls.
actions: Inspect the family graph. Characterize the target binding and calibrate all adopted controls before comparison.

title: Murphy nmos/cmos: implicit common-mode resonance from coupled magnetics
summary: A coupled magnetic network supplies differential and common-mode resonances. Auxiliary capacitance adjusts the return; core width is the main power knob.
actions: Inspect the family graph. Characterize the target binding and calibrate all adopted controls before comparison.

title: Lim inverse-F: drain-gate multimode waveform shaping
summary: Drain-gate multimode feedback shapes the drain waveform. The relevant harmonic port must follow the actual connections, rather than a generic output common-mode assumption.
actions: Inspect the family graph. Characterize the target binding and calibrate all adopted controls before comparison.

title: Guo wideband harmonic shaping: fixed head, no aux
summary: Fixed coupled branches implement broadband harmonic shaping. Only the main tuning control is independent; gate bias controls power.
actions: Inspect the family graph. Characterize the target binding and calibrate all adopted controls before comparison.

title: Du dual-core autotracking: shared capacitance tracks the 2f mode
summary: Two cores share tuning capacitance. Verify intended-mode startup and mode separation; no independent auxiliary control is assumed.
actions: Inspect the family graph. Characterize the target binding and calibrate all adopted controls before comparison.

title: Class-B comparison baseline
summary: A cross-coupled core with optional tail bias is a comparison baseline. Match frequency, power and tank conditions before comparing noise.
actions: Inspect the family graph. Characterize the target binding and calibrate all adopted controls before comparison.
